subtitle: Master compression to control dynamics, enhance sustain, and improve your overall guitar sound

introduction.title: Understanding Compression
introduction.text: Compression is one of the most fundamental yet misunderstood effects in guitar playing. While it may seem transparent compared to distortion or delay, compression profoundly affects your guitar's dynamics, sustain, and overall feel. It can make your playing more consistent, enhance sustain, and create the kind of polished, professional sound heard on countless recordings.
introduction.quote: Compression doesn't just control volume—it shapes the very character of your attack, sustain, and release, making it one of the most powerful tools for crafting your personal guitar sound.

cards.title: The Process
cards.description: Compression reduces the dynamic range of your guitar signal by automatically lowering the volume of loud signals and raising the volume of quiet signals. This creates more consistent levels while affecting the attack and sustain characteristics.
items: 1. Signal exceeds the threshold level
2. Compressor reduces gain by the ratio amount
3. Attack time determines how quickly compression starts
4. Release time controls how quickly it stops
5. Make-up gain compensates for level reduction

cards.title: Musical Effects
items: More consistent picking dynamics
Enhanced sustain on single notes
Tighter, more focused sound
Better balance in complex playing
Increased perceived loudness

cards.title: Threshold
cards.description: Sets the level where compression begins. Signals above this level get compressed; signals below pass through unaffected.

fields.label: High threshold
fields.value: Only peaks get compressed

fields.label: Medium threshold
fields.value: Most normal playing compressed

fields.label: Low threshold
fields.value: Everything gets compressed

fields.label: Musical Impact
fields.value: Higher = more dynamic range preserved. Lower = more consistent, controlled sound. Affects how much your playing dynamics come through.

fields.label: Tip
fields.value: Start with a medium threshold and adjust based on your playing strength.

cards.title: Ratio
cards.description: Determines how much the signal is reduced once it exceeds the threshold. Expressed as a ratio like 4:1, meaning 4dB input creates 1dB output above threshold.

fields.label: 2:1 to 4:1
fields.value: Gentle, musical compression

fields.label: 4:1 to 8:1
fields.value: Noticeable, controlled compression
Heavy limiting, dramatic effect

fields.label: Musical Applications
fields.value: Low ratios = transparent level control. Medium ratios = classic guitar compression. High ratios = special effects, country "squash".

fields.label: Sweet Spot
fields.value: 3:1 to 6:1 works for most guitar applications.

cards.title: Attack & Release
cards.description: Attack: How quickly compression starts after threshold is exceeded. Release: How quickly compression stops after signal drops below threshold.

fields.label: Fast Attack (0.1-1ms)
fields.value: Catches note attacks, smooths picking

fields.label: Medium Attack (1-10ms)
fields.value: Balanced, musical response

fields.label: Slow Attack (10ms+)
fields.value: Preserves pick attack transients

fields.label: Fast Release (10-100ms)
fields.value: Quick recovery, can sound pumpy

fields.label: Medium Release (100ms-1s)
fields.value: Natural, musical decay

fields.label: Slow Release (1s+)
fields.value: Sustained, smooth release

fields.label: Pro Tip
fields.value: Match release time to the tempo and style of your music.

cards.title: Optical Compressors
cards.description: Use a light source and photocell to control gain reduction. The brighter the light, the more compression.

fields.label: Characteristics
fields.value: Smooth musical compression, slow natural attack and release, transparent when set conservatively, vintage warmth and character

fields.label: Best For
fields.value: Clean rhythm guitar, jazz and blues, subtle dynamics control, recording applications

fields.label: Famous Examples
fields.value: LA-2A, Empress Compressor, Origin Cali76

cards.title: VCA Compressors
cards.description: Voltage Controlled Amplifier uses a control voltage to adjust gain reduction with precise timing.

fields.label: Characteristics
fields.value: Fast precise response, detailed parameter control, can be transparent or aggressive, consistent repeatable results

fields.label: Best For
fields.value: Studio recording, precise dynamics control, modern country guitar, professional applications

fields.label: Famous Examples
fields.value: DBX 160X, Boss CS-2, Keeley Compressor Pro

cards.title: FET Compressors
cards.description: Field Effect Transistor controls gain reduction, often with aggressive, punchy character.

fields.label: Characteristics
fields.value: Fast attack aggressive sound, colored characterful compression, punchy in-your-face response, often simpler controls

fields.label: Best For
fields.value: Rock and punk guitar, aggressive rhythm parts, adding sustain to solos, vintage-style compression

fields.label: Famous Examples
fields.value: 1176, Ross Compressor, MXR Dyna Comp

cards.title: Country Guitar
items: Heavy compression (6:1-10:1 ratio)
Fast attack to control pick dynamics
Medium release for sustain
Creates the classic "Nashville" squash
Makes chicken picking more consistent

cards.title: Jazz Guitar
items: Light compression (2:1-3:1 ratio)
Slow attack to preserve note character
Slow release for natural decay
Maintains dynamic expression
Evens out fingerpicking variations

cards.title: Funk/R&B
items: Medium compression (4:1-6:1 ratio)
Fast attack for tight rhythm
Fast release for punchy response
Emphasizes percussive playing
Works great with clean tones

cards.title: Blues Guitar
items: Subtle compression (2:1-4:1 ratio)
Medium attack to keep some dynamics
Slow release for singing sustain
Enhances bends and vibrato
Maintains expressive playing

cards.title: Rock/Metal
items: Moderate compression (3:1-6:1 ratio)
Medium attack for controlled aggression
Medium release for sustain without muddiness
Tightens palm muting
Enhances lead guitar sustain

cards.title: Ambient/Post-Rock
items: Light to medium compression (2:1-5:1)
Slow attack to preserve swells
Very slow release for extended sustain
Supports volume swells and ambient textures
Works well with reverb and delay

cards.title: "Chicken Pickin'" - Country Guitar Style
cards.description: Artists: Brad Paisley, Keith Urban, Brent Mason

fields.label: Compression Settings
fields.value: Heavy ratio (8:1-10:1), fast attack, medium release, high make-up gain

fields.label: Musical Effect
fields.value: Creates consistent pick attack, emphasizes string snaps and muting, allows complex fingerpicking patterns, signature country "squash" sound

cards.title: "Sultans of Swing" - Dire Straits
cards.description: Subtle compression on Mark Knopfler's fingerpicked guitar

fields.label: Compression Settings
fields.value: Light ratio (3:1-4:1), medium attack, slow release, conservative threshold

fields.label: Musical Effect
fields.value: Evens out fingerpicking dynamics, maintains natural expression, creates smooth singing sustain, transparent musical compression

cards.title: "Comfortably Numb" Solo - Pink Floyd
cards.description: Moderate compression enhancing David Gilmour's sustain

fields.label: Compression Settings
fields.value: Medium ratio (4:1-6:1), slow attack, slow release, moderate threshold

fields.label: Musical Effect
fields.value: Extends note sustain dramatically, preserves note attack character, supports expressive bends and vibrato, creates singing emotional tone

cards.title: What to Avoid
items: Over-compressing and losing all dynamics
Using compression to fix poor playing technique
Setting attack too fast and losing pick attack
Not compensating with make-up gain
Using the same settings for all playing styles
Ignoring how compression affects your amp's distortion

cards.title: Best Practices
items: Start with gentle settings and gradually increase
Listen to how compression affects your playing feel
Adjust settings based on musical context
Use your ears, not just visual meter indicators
Consider compression's interaction with other effects
Practice playing with and without compression

cards.title: Serial Compression
cards.description: Using multiple compressors in series for different purposes
items: First compressor: Fast attack, controls peaks
Second compressor: Slow attack, adds sustain
Each does a specific job without overworking
More natural-sounding than extreme single compression

cards.title: Parallel Compression
cards.description: Blending heavily compressed and uncompressed signals
items: Maintains natural dynamics while adding sustain
Heavily compress one signal path
Blend with original uncompressed signal
Best of both worlds: punch and sustain

exercises.title: Exercise 1: Attack Time Comparison
items: Play the same chord progression with different attack settings
Fast attack (0.1ms): Notice how pick attack is smoothed
Medium attack (5ms): Balanced response
Slow attack (20ms): Pick attack preserved, sustain enhanced
Pay attention to how each setting affects the character and feel of your playing

exercises.title: Exercise 2: Dynamic Range Exercise
items: Practice playing with varying pick attack strengths
Very soft picking → medium → aggressive attack
Notice how compression affects the relationship between these levels
Try this with different ratio settings (2:1, 6:1, 10:1)
Observe how higher ratios reduce the difference between soft and hard picking

exercises.title: Exercise 3: Musical Context Practice
items: Practice the same musical phrase in different styles
Country: Heavy compression, fast attack, chicken picking
Jazz: Light compression, slow attack, fingerpicking
Blues: Medium compression, medium attack, expressive bends
Funk: Punchy compression, fast attack/release, percussive style
